subject: Submission route decision: header token and multi-PO invoice handling
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@blueforge.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: billing@blueforge.com
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Vendor onboarding — preferred submission route & sample fields

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the kickoff call last week. We are getting our billing pipeline ready for Redwood and need a couple quick clarifications before we complete the onboarding form. Two questions: 1) preferred submission route — your team mentioned a portal token flow, but our ERP cannot push to external portals without a middleware project; we typically send invoices via SMTP to a billing inbox. Is that acceptable? 2) field mapping — do you require a CSV with a specific header row (line items in separate rows) or do you accept a single PDF with PO numbers in the body?

I attached a sample PDF of one of our invoices and a short CSV extract to show how our system emits line items. (Attachments: sample_invoice_blueforge_0412.pdf, blueforge_sample_rows.csv)

If email is acceptable, what subject convention should we use so your ingestion can auto-route and PO-stamp? Also: can we include multiple PO numbers on a single invoice (we batch shipments across POs)?

Appreciate the guidance — want to avoid reworks once we go live.

Best,
Samir Patel
Billing Ops | Blueforge Systems
Phone: +1 415-555-0198

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@blueforge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Vendor onboarding — preferred submission route & sample fields

Samir — thanks for the clear note and the attachments. Quick answers up front: we prefer the portal for lower ingestion latency and stronger PO-linking, but we can accept SMTP/email as a fallback if portal integration is not feasible in your timeframe.

Two operational constraints to keep in mind if you opt for email:
- Subject token: include "RBW-<vendor-token>-<vendor-id>" in the subject line (we'll provide the vendor-token after onboarding). Example: "RBW-VEND123-Blueforge". This triggers automated routing and ACKs.
- CSV layout: we can process either (a) one-line-per-lineitem CSV with a header row, or (b) a single PDF attachment with readable PO references. For CSVs please include headers: invoice_number, invoice_date (YYYY-MM-DD), po_number, line_description, qty, unit_price, tax_amount, line_total, currency.

On multiple POs per invoice: supported, but they must be separated into separate CSV lines and each line must contain the po_number field. If you send a single PDF with multiple POs, our invoice ops team will route to manual review which may delay processing.

I've attached our vendor-onboarding-form (see onboarding checklist tab) — fill that out and we'll issue a vendor-token for subject routing.

Next steps: if you want to go portal, let us know and I’ll loop in operations to share the API token instructions. If you need to proceed with SMTP, confirm you can add the RBW token in the subject and follow the CSV header above.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik — the guidance is helpful. A couple follow-ups from our side:

1) We can populate the subject token, but the token will be appended by our AP middleware (so sometimes it appears at the end of the subject). Is position-sensitive parsing required or do you look for the token anywhere in the subject?

2) Sample CSV rows (we exported a snippet):
invoice_number,invoice_date,po_number,line_description,qty,unit_price,tax_amount,line_total,currency
INV-2026-0412,2026-12-01,PO-98765,Widget A,10,25.00,0.00,250.00,USD
INV-2026-0412,2026-12-01,PO-98766,Widget B,4,75.00,0.00,300.00,USD

3) We sometimes bundle freight/service lines without a PO (freight line). How should non-PO lines be encoded so your system does not attempt PO-matching?

4) Attachments: we will supply one PDF of the consolidated invoice plus a single CSV for line-level detail. Is that acceptable?

Appreciate quick confirmation — we want minimal manual back-and-forth.

Best,
Samir

Hi Samir — looping in with the final onboarding decision from ProcureOps. Thanks for the sample rows — they map cleanly. Final guidance below so you can finish the form and start sending invoices: 

1) Token parsing: not position-sensitive. Our inbox parser searches the entire subject and the first 5KB of the message body for the vendor token string. Either "RBW-VEND123-Blueforge" anywhere in the subject is fine. If your middleware appends it at the end that's acceptable.

2) CSV + PDF combo: accepted. Operational expectation: send a consolidated PDF (human-readable proof) plus a CSV containing line-level rows. The CSV must use the header row Karthik listed. Non-PO lines: set po_number field to "NA" and include a line_type column with values {"goods","service","freight"}. We'll ignore PO-matching for lines where po_number == "NA" and line_type == "freight" or "service".

3) Multi-PO invoices: allowed as long as each PO appears on its own CSV line. The invoice_number should be identical across lines so we can reconcile the attachment PDF.

4) Acknowledgement SLA: once an email is received with a valid token + CSV header, our system will send an automated receipt ACK within 30 minutes. If manual review is required (e.g., PDF only with multiple POs and no CSV), ACK may be delayed up to 48 hours.

5) Security & attachments: maximum single attachment size 10MB. If you need SFTP for larger files, let us know and Ops will provision a temporary SFTP endpoint.

6) Next items for you: please complete the vendor-onboarding-form (attached) and sign the W9 via DocuSign (link below). Once we receive the completed form we will create your vendor record and reply with the RBW vendor-token.

Onboarding form: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cOnboardingBlueforge
W9 (DocuSign): https://www.docusign.com/blueforge/w9

If you'd like, Vanessa will schedule a brief handoff call to verify CSV export settings.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
